narrative: 从地面看去，一次行走就是一连串鞋底的画面。拖曳的大衣下摆、一个车轮、掉落的枪、如蛇一般贴地的街景视角：地面成为前景，建筑则在其上方变得高大。
西部片和赛车片常用这种机位，因为决定往往就落在地面上。虫眼视角（Worm's-Eye View）是它的近亲，会一直向上看，直到街道消失，只剩下天顶。
低角度（Low Angle）可以从腰部高度拍摄，完全不触及地面。腰部机位（Hip Level）则仍然属于手和枪套的领域。
贴地机位是把摄影机立在地板上的一种支撑方式。
how: 把摄影机放在低位云台、沙袋上，或是挖出的一个坑里，让传感器距离地面只有几厘米。广角镜头会夸大近处靴子的体积和远处地平线的距离感。
你可以沿着地面平视（轨道、轮胎、衣摆），也可以向上倾斜（让大衣填满天空）。近景中要保留沙砾、水渍或尘土，这才能让机位的高度被观众感知到。
提示词：ground-level camera, lens nearly on the floor, boots and trailing coat, horizon very low.
when: 当故事是从地面开始讲起时使用：徒步抵达、一辆车、倒在路上的一具身体。具体场景：靴子踏上尘土飞扬的街道，大衣下摆出现在近景，小镇在远处渐渐显现。
不要把它当作行走对话场景的默认机位，那应该用肩高机位（Shoulder Level）或平视（Eye Level）。
vs: 虫眼视角（Worm's-Eye View）是从同样的高度急剧向上看，直到垂直线全部向内收拢、地平线消失。低角度（Low Angle）只是从低于眼睛的位置向上倾斜拍摄，并不要求镜头必须贴地。
腰部机位（Hip Level）位于腰带高度，让手始终处在对焦平面内。正顶俯拍（Overhead Top-Down）则是另一个极端：地面变成一张平面图，而不是前景。
examples_film: 《西部往事》（Once Upon a Time in the West）让车站的木板、铁轨和靴子主导了整个开场，地面本身就是时间的延展。《亡命驾驶》（Drive）则让车、沥青和鞋子始终留在近景中，让街道成为整个世界。
可以借鉴这种低位支撑机位，以及贴近地面的质感处理。
mistakes: 最常被搞混的是从跪姿高度拍摄的低角度（Low Angle），地面干净、脸部完整入镜。识别标志：没有贴地质感，没有靴子，摄影机明显高于膝盖。
修正方法：镜头几乎贴地，前景中的沙砾或路面要清晰锐利。如果画面里只剩下鼻孔和天空，那你已经偏向了虫眼视角（Worm's-Eye View）。

faq.q: 电影中的贴地机位是什么？
faq.a: 贴地机位是把镜头几乎放在地面上拍摄。靴子、衣摆、车轮和路面成为近景的主体；整个世界仿佛从泥土中升起。

faq.q: 贴地机位与虫眼视角的区别
faq.a: 贴地机位是一种高度设定：摄影机放在地面上，常常沿着靴子平视，或急剧向上看向一件大衣。虫眼视角则是在这个高度基础上做出的极端向上倾斜，垂直线彻底收拢，几乎看不到街道的地平线。

faq.q: 什么时候应该使用贴地机位？
faq.a: 当地面本身就是这场戏的一部分时使用：行走、车辆、掉落的物品、西部片式的抵达场景。不要把它用在普通的坐着对话场景中。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写贴地机位的提示词？
faq.a: 可以这样写：Ground-level camera, lens nearly on the floor, boots and trailing coat in the near field, horizon low. 并说明镜头是沿着地面平视，还是急剧向上看。

narrative: From the dirt, a walk is a sequence of soles. A coat trailing, a wheel, a dropped gun, a snake's view of a street: the floor is the foreground and architecture goes large above it.
Westerns and car films live here because the ground is where decisions land. Worm's-Eye View is the cousin that looks straight up until there is no street, only a zenith.
Low Angle can be shot from the waist and never touch the floor. Hip Level still belongs to hands and holsters.
Ground-level is the pedestal on the boards.
how: Set the camera on a low plate, a sandbag, or a hole so the sensor is centimeters from the ground. A wide lens exaggerates the near boots and the far horizon.
You may look along the floor (track, tire, hem) or tilt up (a coat filling the sky). Keep grit, wet, or dust in the near field; that is how the height reads.
Prompt: ground-level camera, lens nearly on the floor, boots and trailing coat, horizon very low.
when: Use it when the story starts from the dirt: an arrival on foot, a car, a body on the road. Concrete beat: boots stepping onto a dusty street, coat hem in the near field, town rising beyond.
Do not use it as the default for a walking conversation; that is Shoulder Level or Eye Level.
vs: Worm's-Eye View looks sharply up from this height until verticals collapse and the horizon dies. Low Angle is a pitch from below the eyes, not a requirement that the lens kiss the floor.
Hip Level sits at belt height so hands stay in the plane of focus. Overhead Top-Down is the opposite pole: the floor as a plan, not as a foreground.
examples_film: Once Upon a Time in the West lets the station boards, tracks, and boots own the opening; the ground is duration. Drive keeps cars, asphalt, and shoes in the near field so the street is the world.
Borrow the low pedestal and the near-ground texture.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Low Angle from kneeling height with a clean floor and a full face. Tell: no near-ground texture, no boots, camera clearly at knee-plus.
Fix: lens nearly on the floor, grit or pavement sharp in the foreground. If the shot is only nostrils and sky, you drifted into Worm's-Eye View.

faq.q: What is ground level in film?
faq.a: A ground-level shot places the lens almost on the floor. Boots, hems, wheels, and pavement become the near subject; the world rises from the dirt.

Ground level is a height: camera on the floor, often looking along boots or steeply up a coat. Worm's-eye view is an extreme upward pitch from that height, verticals collapsing, almost no street horizon.

faq.q: When should I use ground level?
faq.a: Use it when the ground is part of the beat: a walk, a car, a dropped object, a Western arrival. Do not use it for ordinary seated talk.

faq.q: How do I prompt ground level for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Ground-level camera, lens nearly on the floor, boots and trailing coat in the near field, horizon low. Say whether it looks along the dirt or steeply up.
